verdict.root_cause: At 07:42:01Z platform-automation lowered adservice's container memory limit to 256m (tr_5621f4cd4674). Within seconds adservice stopped serving: logs switch from ad-request handling to bare JVM/OTel-agent startup banners repeating eleven-plus times through 07:49 on a ~63s backoff, never reaching readiness (tr_83cad89a01f8). The JVM cannot complete init inside the new ceiling, so the container is killed and restarted repeatedly. With no ready pod, adservice's endpoints vanish - its call-count series is entirely absent (tr_1d5d97a07362) - and frontend's gRPC client fails DNS resolution of the adservice target on 9555 with code 14 UNAVAILABLE (tr_8b0fa430b324). Impact is confined to the ad path: only AdService/GetAds spans error, sub-millisecond, while checkout, cart and catalog traces complete cleanly (tr_5dcff80b14aa), matching frontend's partial ~7.4% peak error ratio (tr_7e1118017a6b) with no frontend change recorded (tr_c47d16482d7f).
verdict.reasoning: The limit reduction at 07:42:01 and the first crash-loop banner at 07:42:17 are tightly coupled in time. Each cycle dies during JVM/agent init with no application log line and a regular ~63s backoff, which is a startup resource kill, not a hang, drain, or deploy (no image or scaling event recorded). The empty adservice metric series is missing telemetry, not health - the trap seen in the cart-redis and cart-bad-image past incidents. Frontend's DNS-resolution UNAVAILABLE errors naming only adservice:9555 are the expected downstream symptom of endpoint withdrawal, and the narrow trace blast radius plus sub-10% error ratio confirm a single-dependency partial failure. Class is resource_exhaustion because the running mechanism is a process killed for exceeding a memory ceiling; the edit is how it started. Restart is useless - the pod already restarts itself every ~63s - so the fix is restoring the prior memory limit.
open_questions: No direct runtime confirmation of OOM kill (exit 137/OOMKilled, memory working-set metrics); exhaustion is inferred from change timing plus JVM-init crash loop.
The prior memory limit is unrecorded, so the correct value to restore is unknown, and it is unclear whether platform-automation will re-apply 256m.
loadgenerator alerted at 07:45:15 but was never dispatched on, and change logs for the other five services were not queried, so a concurrent second factor is not excluded.
